addedLines: - academic-research-skills:report_compiler_agent: Transforms research findings into polished APA 7.0 academic reports; activated in Phase 4 and Phase 6 (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)

- academic-research-skills:research_architect_agent: Designs the methodological blueprint; selects research paradigm, method, data strategy, and analytical framework (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)
- academic-research-skills:synthesis_agent: Integrates findings across sources, resolves evidence conflicts, and maps knowledge gaps (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

1 # ResearchGPT — Master Specification & Build Handoff 2 3 > **Purpose of this file.** Single source of truth for the ResearchGPT project. Written to be handed to an autonomous coding agent (Claude Code). It contains the research framing, system architecture, agent contracts, data models, repo layout, build order, and acceptance criteria. Place at repo root; reference it from `CLAUDE.md` with `See RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md for full system spec.` 4 > 5 > **Status:** Literature review complete. Implementation not yet started. Build from Phase 0. 6 7 --- 8 9 ## 0. TL;DR for the implementing agent 10 11 Build a **multi-agent agentic RAG system for automated literature review**. Six agents — Planner, Retriever, Extractor, Verifier, Critic, Writer — orchestrated as a **LangGraph** state machine with a **critic-driven feedback loop**. Input: a research question. Output: a structured, fully-cited literature review (Markdown + DOCX + BibTeX) plus a per-paper structured insight table. 12 13 Non-negotiables: 14 15 1. **Every claim in the output must be traceable to a retrieved chunk.** Unverifiable claims are dropped, not softened. 16 2. **Peer-reviewed (Scopus/IEEE/ACL) sources rank above preprints.** Preprints are permitted as secondary technical references and must be labelled as such. 17 3. **The graph is agentic, not a fixed pipeline.** The Critic can send control back to Planner or Retriever. Loop bound: 3 iterations. 18 4. **Model-agnostic LLM layer.** All calls route through one adapter so the backend can be swapped (GPT/Claude/Gemma-local) without touching agent logic. 19 20 --- 21 22 ## 1. Research framing 23 24 ### 1.1 Problem 25 Manual literature review is slow, inconsistent, and does not scale with publication volume. Existing RAG systems answer questions over papers but do not produce *review-grade* artefacts: they lack per-paper structured extraction, cross-paper synthesis, and verifiable citation grounding. 26 27 ### 1.2 Base paper 28 **Aytar et al. (2025)**, *Natural Language Processing Journal* (Elsevier, Scopus-indexed) — RAG-based literature assistance. 29 30 ### 1.3 Extension narrative (must hold in the paper) 31 The system must be demonstrably more capable than the base paper along articulable dimensions: 32 33 | Dimension | Base paper | ResearchGPT | 34 |---|---|---| 35 | Retrieval control | Fixed single-pass pipeline | Agentic, replanning, multi-round query reformulation | 36 | Per-paper output | Free-text summary | Structured 4-field schema: Methodology / Advantages / Disadvantages / Critique | 37 | Cross-paper reasoning | Absent or shallow | Explicit thematic clustering + contradiction and gap detection | 38 | Verification | Implicit / none | Dedicated Verifier agent; claim→span grounding with support scores | 39 | Quality control | None | Critic agent with bounded replan loop and stop criteria | 40 | Source discipline | Mixed | Venue-tier ranking; preprints demoted and flagged | 41 42 ### 1.4 Contributions to claim 43 1. A six-agent agentic RAG architecture for end-to-end automated literature review. 44 2. A structured per-paper insight schema enabling tabular, comparable extraction at scale. 45 3. A verification layer providing claim-level citation grounding with quantified support. 46 4. A critic-driven bounded feedback loop for coverage and quality control. 47 5. An evaluation protocol for review-generation quality (coverage, grounding, citation accuracy). 48 49 ### 1.5 Literature review assets (already produced — do not redo) 50 - 25-paper survey organised into six thematic clusters (Word doc). 51 - 10-paper IEEE addendum (Word doc). 52 - Citations verified with DOIs/URLs. Notable resolutions: Du et al. (ICML) via PMLR; Self-RAG via OpenReview; Adaptive-RAG via ACL Anthology. 53 54 ### 1.6 Thematic clusters (reuse as taxonomy in code and paper) 55 `C1` RAG foundations · `C2` Agentic & self-reflective RAG · `C3` Multi-agent LLM systems · `C4` Scientific document understanding & IE · `C5` Automated survey/review generation · `C6` Evaluation, grounding & hallucination detection 56 57 --- 58 59 ## 2. Technology stack 60 61 | Layer | Choice | Notes | 62 |---|---|---| 63 | Orchestration | **LangGraph** | Stateful graph, conditional edges, checkpointing | 64 | Tooling / chains | **LangChain** | Loaders, splitters, retrievers, tool wrappers | 65 | LLM adapter | **LiteLLM** | One interface; swap providers via config | 66 | Local inference | **Ollama / ChatOllama**, vLLM, LM Studio | Gemma is the local candidate — *validate architecture on a strong hosted model first, then swap* | 67 | Vector store | **Chroma** (dev) → **Qdrant** (scale) | Persist to `./data/vectorstore` | 68 | Lexical index | **BM25** (`rank_bm25`) | For hybrid retrieval | 69 | Reranker | `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` (cross-encoder) | CPU-tolerable; optional flag | 70 | Embeddings | `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` or `text-embedding-3-large` | Config-selectable | 71 | Validation | **Pydantic v2** | All agent I/O is typed | 72 | PDF parsing | **PyMuPDF** + **GROBID** (optional) | GROBID for section/reference structure | 73 | Doc output | **python-docx**, Markdown, **BibTeX** | IEEE citation style | 74 | API / UI | FastAPI + Streamlit | UI is optional, Phase 6 | 75 | Tracing | LangSmith or local JSONL run log | Required for the evaluation section | 76 | Testing | pytest + `vcrpy` cassettes | Deterministic tests, no live API in CI | 77 78 **Sources:** Semantic Scholar API, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, PubMed, ACL Anthology, OpenReview, PMLR, IEEE Xplore, Scopus. Free/keyless first (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv); keyed sources behind feature flags. 79 80 --- 81 82 ## 3. Execution sequence 247 248 ```mermaid 249 sequenceDiagram 250 autonumber 251 actor U as Researcher 252 participant G as LangGraph 253 participant P as Planner 254 participant R as Retriever 255 participant S as Sources + Index 256 participant E as Extractor 257 participant V as Verifier 258 participant C as Critic 259 participant W as Writer 260 261 U->>G: research_question, constraints 262 G->>P: plan(question) 263 P-->>G: sub_questions[], search_plan[], taxonomy 264 265 loop per sub-question 266 G->>R: retrieve(sub_question) 267 R->>S: federated search + dedup by DOI 268 S-->>R: candidate papers 269 R->>S: ingest, chunk, embed, hybrid search 270 S-->>R: ranked chunks 271 R-->>G: papers[], chunks[] 272 end 273 274 G->>E: extract(papers, chunks) 275 E-->>G: PaperInsight[] with span refs 276 277 G->>V: verify(insights, chunks) 278 V-->>G: verdicts, support_scores, unsupported[] 279 280 G->>C: critique(state) 281 alt coverage gap 282 C-->>G: RETRIEVE with widened queries 283 G->>R: re-retrieve 284 else plan flawed 285 C-->>G: REPLAN 286 G->>P: replan with feedback 287 else approved or max_iterations 288 C-->>G: WRITE 289 end 290 291 G->>W: synthesize(verified state) 292 W-->>G: review.md, insights.csv, refs.bib 293 G-->>U: artefacts + trace.jsonl 294 ``` 295 296 --- 297 298 ## 6. Data flow through state 299 300 ```mermaid 301 flowchart LR 302 Q["research_question"] --> SQ["sub_questions[]"] 303 SQ --> QP["search_plan[] - query, sources, filters"] 304 QP --> CP["candidate_papers[] - raw hits"] 305 CP --> DP["deduped_papers[] - DOI keyed"] 306 DP --> SP["screened_papers[] - inclusion criteria"] 307 SP --> CH["chunks[] - with span offsets"] 308 CH --> RC["ranked_chunks[] - hybrid + rerank"] 309 RC --> PI["paper_insights[] - 4-field schema"] 310 PI --> VC["verified_claims[] - score, evidence"] 311 VC --> TH["themes[] - cluster, contradictions, gaps"] 312 TH --> DR["draft_sections[]"] 313 DR --> FN["final_review + refs.bib + insights.csv"] 314 315 VC -.->|"below threshold"| QP 316 TH -.->|"thin coverage"| SQ 317 ``` 318 319 --- 320 321 ## 7. Agent contracts 322 323 Every agent subclasses `Agent` in `agents/base.py` and implements `run(state: ReviewState) -> dict` returning a **partial state update only**. Agents never mutate state in place. Every agent logs `{agent, iteration, input_hash, output_summary, tokens, latency}` to the trace. 324 325 ### 7.1 Planner 326 - **In:** `research_question`, `constraints`, optional `critic_feedback` 327 - **Out:** `sub_questions[]` (4–8), `search_plan[]`, `taxonomy` (seeded from C1–C6), `inclusion_criteria` 328 - **Behaviour:** decomposes by facet (method / application / evaluation / limitation). Emits per-sub-question source priority and year filters. On replan, must *change* the plan — record a diff, never re-emit an identical plan. 329 330 ### 7.2 Retriever 331 - **In:** `search_plan[]` 332 - **Out:** `papers[]`, `chunks[]`, `retrieval_log` 333 - **Behaviour:** 334 1. Federated search across enabled connectors; normalise to `Paper`. 335 2. Dedup by DOI → normalised title+year fallback. 336 3. Screen against `inclusion_criteria`; drop out-of-scope early (cheap LLM or heuristic). 337 4. Fetch OA PDFs where available; parse, chunk, embed, index. 338 5. Hybrid retrieve: dense (k=30) + BM25 (k=30) → RRF fuse → cross-encoder rerank → top-k=12 per sub-question. 339 6. Assign `venue_tier` via Citation Service. 340 - **Rule:** never fabricate metadata. A field that cannot be resolved is `None`, not guessed. 341 342 ### 7.3 Extractor 343 - **In:** `papers[]`, `chunks[]` 344 - **Out:** `paper_insights[]` 345 - **Schema per paper (the four-field standard):** `methodology`, `advantages`, `disadvantages`, `critique` — plus `datasets`, `metrics`, `results`, `limitations`, `evidence_spans[]`. 346 - **Rule:** every field carries `evidence_spans` (chunk_id + char offsets). No span → field is `null` with `extraction_note`. 347 348 ### 7.4 Verifier 349 - **In:** `paper_insights[]`, `chunks[]` 350 - **Out:** `verified_claims[]`, `unsupported_claims[]`, `grounding_score` 351 - **Behaviour:** decompose each insight into atomic claims; retrieve supporting evidence for each; NLI-style judgement → `SUPPORTED` / `PARTIAL` / `UNSUPPORTED` / `CONTRADICTED` with `support_score ∈ [0,1]`. Threshold default `0.7`. Cross-paper contradiction detection produces `contradiction_pairs[]`. 352 - **Rule:** unsupported claims are **removed** from the write path and logged — never hedged into the output. 353 354 ### 7.5 Critic 355 - **In:** full state 356 - **Out:** `decision ∈ {WRITE, RETRIEVE, REPLAN}`, `feedback`, `coverage_report` 357 - **Checks:** sub-question coverage ≥ 80%; ≥ `min_papers` (default 20) retained; grounding_score ≥ 0.75; no sub-question with < 2 supporting papers; venue-tier mix acceptable; recency window satisfied. 358 - **Loop control:** `max_iterations = 3`. On the final iteration force `WRITE` and record unresolved gaps in a *Limitations* section rather than looping forever. 359 360 ### 7.6 Writer 361 - **In:** verified state 362 - **Out:** `review.md`, `review.docx`, `insights.csv`, `refs.bib` 363 - **Structure:** Abstract · Introduction · Methodology of the review · Thematic sections (one per cluster) · Comparative insight table · Contradictions & open problems · Research gaps · Conclusion · References. 364 - **Rules:** IEEE numeric citation style `[n]`. Every non-trivial sentence carries ≥1 citation. Preprints marked `[preprint]` in the reference list. No sentence may be written that is not backed by a `verified_claim`. 365 366 --- 367 368 ## 8. Core data models (`core/models.py`) 369 370 ```python 371 from typing import Literal, Optional 372 from pydantic import BaseModel, Field 373 374 VenueTier = Literal["scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"] 375 Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"] 376 Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"] 377 378 class Paper(BaseModel): 379 paper_id: str 380 doi: Optional[str] = None 381 title: str 382 authors: list[str] = [] 383 year: Optional[int] = None 384 venue: Optional[str] = None 385 venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown" 386 abstract: Optional[str] = None 387 url: Optional[str] = None 388 pdf_path: Optional[str] = None 389 source: str # openalex | s2 | arxiv | acl | ieee | scopus ... 390 citation_count: Optional[int] = None 391 is_preprint: bool = False 392 393 class Chunk(BaseModel): 394 chunk_id: str 395 paper_id: str 396 text: str 397 section: Optional[str] = None # abstract | methods | results | ... 398 start_char: int 399 end_char: int 400 embedding_id: Optional[str] = None 401 402 class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel): 403 chunk_id: str 404 quote: str 405 start_char: int 406 end_char: int 407 408 class PaperInsight(BaseModel): 409 paper_id: str 410 methodology: Optional[str] = None 411 advantages: Optional[str] = None 412 disadvantages: Optional[str] = None 413 critique: Optional[str] = None 414 datasets: list[str] = [] 415 metrics: list[str] = [] 416 results: Optional[str] = None 417 limitations: Optional[str] = None 418 cluster: Optional[str] = None # C1..C6 419 evidence_spans: list[EvidenceSpan] = [] 420 extraction_note: Optional[str] = None 421 422 class Claim(BaseModel): 423 claim_id: str 424 text: str 425 paper_ids: list[str] 426 verdict: Verdict 427 support_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0) 428 evidence: list[EvidenceSpan] = [] 429 430 class SubQuestion(BaseModel): 431 sq_id: str 432 text: str 433 facet: str # method | application | evaluation | limitation 434 covered: bool = False 435 supporting_paper_ids: list[str] = [] 436 437 class SearchTask(BaseModel): 438 sq_id: str 439 query: str 440 sources: list[str] 441 year_min: Optional[int] = None 442 max_results: int = 25 443 ``` 444 445 ### 8.1 Graph state (`graph/state.py`) 446 447 ```python 448 from typing import Annotated, TypedDict 449 from operator import add 450 451 class ReviewState(TypedDict, total=False): 452 # input 453 research_question: str 454 constraints: dict # years, venues, max_papers, language 455 # planner 456 sub_questions: list[SubQuestion] 457 search_plan: list[SearchTask] 458 inclusion_criteria: list[str] 459 # retriever 460 papers: Annotated[list[Paper], add] 461 chunks: Annotated[list[Chunk], add] 462 retrieval_log: Annotated[list[dict], add] 463 # extractor / verifier 464 paper_insights: list[PaperInsight] 465 verified_claims: list[Claim] 466 unsupported_claims: list[Claim] 467 contradiction_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] 468 grounding_score: float 469 # critic 470 decision: str 471 critic_feedback: str 472 coverage_report: dict 473 iteration: int 474 # writer 475 themes: list[dict] 476 draft_sections: dict 477 final_review: str 478 artefacts: dict 479 ``` 480 481 --- 482 483 ## 9. Graph assembly (`graph/build.py`) 484 485 ```python 486 from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END 487 488 def route_after_critic(state: ReviewState) -> str: 489 if state.get("iteration", 0) >= MAX_ITERATIONS: 490 return "writer" 491 return {"WRITE": "writer", "RETRIEVE": "retriever", "REPLAN": "planner"}[state["decision"]] 492 493 g = StateGraph(ReviewState) 494 g.add_node("planner", planner_node) 495 g.add_node("retriever", retriever_node) 496 g.add_node("extractor", extractor_node) 497 g.add_node("verifier", verifier_node) 498 g.add_node("critic", critic_node) 499 g.add_node("writer", writer_node) 500 501 g.add_edge(START, "planner") 502 g.add_edge("planner", "retriever") 503 g.add_edge("retriever", "extractor") 504 g.add_edge("extractor", "verifier") 505 g.add_edge("verifier", "critic") 506 g.add_conditional_edges("critic", route_after_critic, 507 {"writer": "writer", "retriever": "retriever", "planner": "planner"}) 508 g.add_edge("writer", END) 509 510 app = g.compile(checkpointer=SqliteSaver.from_conn_string("./data/checkpoints.db")) 511 ``` 512 513 State diagram: 514 515 ```mermaid 516 stateDiagram-v2 517 [*] --> Planning 518 Planning --> Retrieving 519 Retrieving --> Extracting 520 Extracting --> Verifying 521 Verifying --> Critiquing 522 Critiquing --> Writing: approved / max iterations 523 Critiquing --> Retrieving: coverage gap 524 Critiquing --> Planning: plan flawed 525 Writing --> [*] 526 ``` 527 528 --- 529 530 ## 10. Repository layout 531 532 ``` 533 researchgpt/ 534 ├── CLAUDE.md 535 ├── RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md 536 ├── pyproject.toml 537 ├── .env.example 538 ├── configs/ 539 │ ├── default.yaml 540 │ ├── local_gemma.yaml 541 │ └── eval.yaml 542 ├── src/researchgpt/ 543 │ ├── core/ llm.py config.py models.py logging.py prompts/ 544 │ ├── data/ ingest.py chunker.py embeddings.py vectorstore.py bm25_index.py metadata_db.py 545 │ ├── tools/ search_sources.py hybrid_retriever.py reranker.py pdf_loader.py citation_tools.py 546 │ ├── agents/ base.py planner.py retriever.py extractor.py verifier.py critic.py writer.py 547 │ ├── graph/ state.py build.py routing.py checkpoint.py 548 │ ├── output/ markdown_writer.py docx_writer.py bibtex_writer.py insight_table.py 549 │ ├── eval/ metrics.py ragas_runner.py ablations.py 550 │ ├── api/ app.py schemas.py 551 │ └── cli.py 552 ├── tests/ unit/ integration/ fixtures/ cassettes/ 553 ├── data/ raw/ pdfs/ vectorstore/ metadata.db checkpoints.db 554 ├── outputs/ runs//{review.md,review.docx,insights.csv,refs.bib,trace.jsonl} 555 └── notebooks/ 01_ingest.ipynb 02_retrieval_eval.ipynb 03_ablations.ipynb 556 ``` 557 558 ### 10.1 Config (`configs/default.yaml`) 559 560 ```yaml 561 llm: 562 provider: openai # openai | anthropic | ollama 563 model: gpt-4o-mini 564 planner_model: gpt-4o # heavier model for planning + critique 565 temperature: 0.1 566 max_tokens: 4096 567 embeddings: 568 model: BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 569 device: cpu 570 retrieval: 571 dense_k: 30 572 sparse_k: 30 573 fusion: rrf 574 rerank: true 575 reranker: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 576 final_k: 12 577 chunk_size: 1200 578 chunk_overlap: 200 579 sources: 580 enabled: [openalex, semantic_scholar, arxiv, crossref] 581 optional: [ieee, scopus, acl, openreview, pmlr] 582 max_per_source: 25 583 review: 584 min_papers: 20 585 max_papers: 60 586 year_min: 2019 587 max_iterations: 3 588 grounding_threshold: 0.7 589 coverage_threshold: 0.8 590 output: 591 citation_style: ieee 592 formats: [markdown, docx, csv, bibtex] 593 ``` 594 595 --- 596 597 ## 11. Retrieval design 598 599 - **Chunking:** section-aware. Split on GROBID/heuristic section boundaries first, then recursive character split at 1200/200. Never merge across papers. Preserve `start_char`/`end_char` for grounding. 600 - **Hybrid search:** dense (cosine) + BM25, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion `score = Σ 1/(60 + rank_i)`. 601 - **Reranking:** cross-encoder over the fused top-60 → top-12. 602 - **Query expansion:** Planner emits 2–3 paraphrases per sub-question; union results before fusion. 603 - **Venue tiering:** boost `scopus_q1 > scopus/ieee/acl > peer_reviewed > preprint`. Applied as a score multiplier, not a hard filter, so strong preprints survive but rank below peer-reviewed work. 604 - **Dedup:** DOI → normalised `title|year` → embedding cosine > 0.97 on title+abstract. 605 606 --- 607 608 ## 12. Evaluation protocol 609 610 | Metric | Definition | Target | 611 |---|---|---| 612 | Retrieval Recall@k | Fraction of gold papers found in top-k | ≥ 0.80 | 613 | Precision@k | Relevant among retrieved | ≥ 0.70 | 614 | Citation accuracy | Citations resolving to a real paper that supports the claim | ≥ 0.95 | 615 | Groundedness | Sentences with ≥1 supporting span | ≥ 0.90 | 616 | Coverage | Sub-questions with ≥2 supporting papers | ≥ 0.80 | 617 | Extraction F1 | Four-field extraction vs. human annotation on 20 papers | ≥ 0.75 | 618 | Hallucination rate | Claims marked UNSUPPORTED that reach output | 0 by construction; report attempts | 619 | Cost / latency | Tokens and wall-clock per review | Reported | 620 621 **Ablations (required for the paper):** 622 1. Full system (all six agents). 623 2. − Critic loop (single pass). 624 3. − Verifier (no grounding filter). 625 4. − Agentic planning (single flat query). 626 5. − Hybrid retrieval (dense only). 627 6. − Reranker. 628 7. Baseline: vanilla RAG ≈ base paper configuration. 629 630 **Human evaluation:** 3 annotators, 5 reviews, 5-point Likert on coverage / correctness / coherence / usefulness; report Krippendorff's α. Also run RAGAS (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall) as an automated cross-check. 631 632 --- 633 634 ## 13. Build order 635 636 | Phase | Deliverable | Done when | 637 |---|---|---| 638 | **0. Scaffold** | Repo, pyproject, config loader, LLM adapter, logging, `Paper`/`Chunk` models, CLI stub | `researchgpt --version` runs; adapter returns a completion from both hosted and Ollama | 639 | **1. Ingestion + index** | Source connectors (OpenAlex, S2, arXiv, Crossref), PDF parse, chunk, embed, Chroma + BM25 | Query returns ranked chunks with correct span offsets | 640 | **2. Hybrid retrieval** | RRF fusion, reranker, venue tiering, dedup | Recall@20 ≥ 0.8 on a 30-paper gold set | 641 | **3. Agents (linear)** | Planner → Retriever → Extractor → Writer wired in LangGraph, no loop | End-to-end run produces a cited draft | 642 | **4. Verification** | Verifier agent, claim decomposition, support scoring, unsupported filtering | Groundedness ≥ 0.9 on a sample | 643 | **5. Agentic loop** | Critic agent, conditional edges, checkpointing, iteration cap | Loop demonstrably triggers and terminates on a deliberately under-covered query | 644 | **6. Output + eval** | DOCX/BibTeX/CSV writers, metrics, ablation runner, optional Streamlit UI | Ablation table reproducible from one command | 645 | **7. Paper support** | Figures from real traces, results tables, reproducibility script | `make reproduce` regenerates all reported numbers | 646 647 --- 648 649 ## 14. Rules for the coding agent 650 651 1. **Typed boundaries.** All agent I/O validates through Pydantic. A validation failure is an error, not a warning. 652 2. **No silent fabrication.** If metadata, a DOI, or a supporting span cannot be resolved, emit `None` and log. Never invent a citation, author, year, or venue. 653 3. **Partial state updates only.** Agents return dicts merged by LangGraph reducers. 654 4. **Prompts live in `core/prompts/` as versioned files**, not inline strings. Each prompt file has a header comment stating its agent, version, and expected output schema. 655 5. **Every LLM call goes through `core/llm.py`.** No direct SDK imports in agent modules. 656 6. **Deterministic tests.** Record fixtures with `vcrpy`; CI never hits a live API or a paid endpoint. 657 7. **Bounded loops.** Any retry, replan, or re-retrieve path must have an explicit cap and a forced exit. 658 8. **Cost guardrails.** Track tokens per run; abort with a clear error above `max_cost_usd` in config. 659 9. **Respect source terms.** Honour rate limits and robots; use official APIs; store only OA PDFs locally. 660 10. **Reproducibility.** Every run writes `outputs/runs//` containing config snapshot, trace, and artefacts. 661 662 --- 663 664 ## 15. Known risks and mitigations 665 666 | Risk | Mitigation | 667 |---|---| 668 | Paywalled PDFs limit full-text extraction | Abstract-only degraded mode; flag `text_availability` per paper and report the split | 669 | API rate limits / key gating (Scopus, IEEE) | Keyless sources are the default path; keyed connectors behind flags | 670 | Loop non-termination or oscillation | Hard `max_iterations`; require plan diff on replan; forced WRITE on final iteration | 671 | Cost blow-up from long contexts | Small model for extraction, large model for planning/critique; rerank before sending to LLM | 672 | Local Gemma underperforms on structured extraction | Validate the architecture on a strong hosted model first; treat local swap as an ablation, not the baseline | 673 | Extraction schema drift across papers | Strict Pydantic schema + retry-with-repair on parse failure, max 2 repairs | 674 | Reviewer objection: "just RAG with extra steps" | Ablations 2–5 exist specifically to quantify each agent's contribution | 675 676 --- 677 678 ## 16. Open decisions 679 680 - Vector store: stay on Chroma or move to Qdrant before Phase 6? 681 - Whether to run GROBID (better structure, heavier setup) or PyMuPDF-only heuristics. 682 - Gemma integration timing — after Phase 5 stabilises, as an ablation row. 683 - Whether the Streamlit UI is in scope for the paper or deferred. 684 685 --- 686 687 *Last updated: 2026-08-06. Amend this file rather than duplicating spec text elsewhere.* 688

# ResearchGPT — Master Specification & Build Handoff > **Purpose of this file.** Single source of truth for the ResearchGPT project. Written to be handed to an autonomous coding agent (Claude Code). It contains the research framing, system architecture, agent contracts, data models, repo layout, build order, and acceptance criteria. Place at repo root; reference it from `CLAUDE.md` with `See RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md for full system spec.` > > **Status:** Literature review complete. Implementation not yet started. Build from Phase 0. --- ## 0. TL;DR for the implementing agent Build a **multi-agent agentic RAG system for automated literature review**. Six agents — Planner, Retriever, Extractor, Verifier, Critic, Writer — orchestrated as a **LangGraph** state machine with a **critic-driven feedback loop**. Input: a research question. Output: a structured, fully-cited literature review (Markdown + DOCX + BibTeX) plus a per-paper structured insight table. Non-negotiables: 1. **Every claim in the output must be traceable to a retrieved chunk.** Unverifiable claims are dropped, not softened. 2. **Peer-reviewed (Scopus/IEEE/ACL) sources rank above preprints.** Preprints are permitted as secondary technical references and must be labelled as such. 3. **The graph is agentic, not a fixed pipeline.** The Critic can send control back to Planner or Retriever. Loop bound: 3 iterations. 4. **Model-agnostic LLM layer.** All calls route through one adapter so the backend can be swapped (GPT/Claude/Gemma-local) without touching agent logic. --- ## 1. Research framing ### 1.1 Problem Manual literature review is slow, inconsistent, and does not scale with publication volume. Existing RAG systems answer questions over papers but do not produce *review-grade* artefacts: they lack per-paper structured extraction, cross-paper synthesis, and verifiable citation grounding. ### 1.2 Base paper **Aytar et al. (2025)**, *Natural Language Processing Journal* (Elsevier, Scopus-indexed) — RAG-based literature assistance. ### 1.3 Extension narrative (must hold in the paper) The system must be demonstrably more capable than the base paper along articulable dimensions: | Dimension | Base paper | ResearchGPT | |---|---|---| | Retrieval control | Fixed single-pass pipeline | Agentic, replanning, multi-round query reformulation | | Per-paper output | Free-text summary | Structured 4-field schema: Methodology / Advantages / Disadvantages / Critique | | Cross-paper reasoning | Absent or shallow | Explicit thematic clustering + contradiction and gap detection | | Verification | Implicit / none | Dedicated Verifier agent; claim→span grounding with support scores | | Quality control | None | Critic agent with bounded replan loop and stop criteria | | Source discipline | Mixed | Venue-tier ranking; preprints demoted and flagged | ### 1.4 Contributions to claim 1. A six-agent agentic RAG architecture for end-to-end automated literature review. 2. A structured per-paper insight schema enabling tabular, comparable extraction at scale. 3. A verification layer providing claim-level citation grounding with quantified support. 4. A critic-driven bounded feedback loop for coverage and quality control. 5. An evaluation protocol for review-generation quality (coverage, grounding, citation accuracy). ### 1.5 Literature review assets (already produced — do not redo) - 25-paper survey organised into six thematic clusters (Word doc). - 10-paper IEEE addendum (Word doc). - Citations verified with DOIs/URLs. Notable resolutions: Du et al. (ICML) via PMLR; Self-RAG via OpenReview; Adaptive-RAG via ACL Anthology. ### 1.6 Thematic clusters (reuse as taxonomy in code and paper) `C1` RAG foundations · `C2` Agentic & self-reflective RAG · `C3` Multi-agent LLM systems · `C4` Scientific document understanding & IE · `C5` Automated survey/review generation · `C6` Evaluation, grounding & hallucination detection --- ## 2. Technology stack | Layer | Choice | Notes | |---|---|---| | Orchestration | **LangGraph** | Stateful graph, conditional edges, checkpointing | | Tooling / chains | **LangChain** | Loaders, splitters, retrievers, tool wrappers | | LLM adapter | **LiteLLM** | One interface; swap providers via config | | Local inference | **Ollama / ChatOllama**, vLLM, LM Studio | Gemma is the local candidate — *validate architecture on a strong hosted model first, then swap* | | Vector store | **Chroma** (dev) → **Qdrant** (scale) | Persist to `./data/vectorstore` | | Lexical index | **BM25** (`rank_bm25`) | For hybrid retrieval | | Reranker | `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` (cross-encoder) | CPU-tolerable; optional flag | | Embeddings | `BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5` or `text-embedding-3-large` | Config-selectable | | Validation | **Pydantic v2** | All agent I/O is typed | | PDF parsing | **PyMuPDF** + **GROBID** (optional) | GROBID for section/reference structure | | Doc output | **python-docx**, Markdown, **BibTeX** | IEEE citation style | | API / UI | FastAPI + Streamlit | UI is optional, Phase 6 | | Tracing | LangSmith or local JSONL run log | Required for the evaluation section | | Testing | pytest + `vcrpy` cassettes | Deterministic tests, no live API in CI | **Sources:** Semantic Scholar API, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, PubMed, ACL Anthology, OpenReview, PMLR, IEEE Xplore, Scopus. Free/keyless first (OpenAlex, Crossref, Semantic Scholar, arXiv); keyed sources behind feature flags. --- ## 3. System architecture ```mermaid flowchart TB U["Researcher: research question + constraints"] subgraph ORCH["LangGraph Orchestrator"] direction TB P["Planner Agent
decompose into sub-questions
build search plan"] R["Retriever Agent
multi-source search
hybrid + rerank"] E["Extractor Agent
per-paper structured insights"] V["Verifier Agent
claim to span grounding"] C["Critic Agent
coverage + quality gate"] W["Writer Agent
synthesis and review draft"] end subgraph SVC["Service Layer"] direction TB LLM["LLM Adapter - LiteLLM
hosted or local Ollama"] IDX["Index Service
Chroma dense + BM25 sparse"] SRC["Source Connectors
OpenAlex, S2, Crossref, arXiv,
ACL, OpenReview, PMLR, IEEE, Scopus"] ING["Ingestion
PDF parse, clean, chunk, embed"] CIT["Citation Service
DOI resolve, venue tier, BibTeX"] end subgraph STORE["Persistence"] direction LR VS[("Vector Store")] BM[("BM25 Index")] MD[("Paper Metadata DB")] RUN[("Run State + Traces")] end OUT["Outputs

Data flow through state ```mermaid flowchart LR Q["research_question"] --> SQ["sub_questions[]"] SQ --> QP["search_plan[] - query, sources, filters"] QP --> CP["candidate_papers[] - raw hits"] CP --> DP["deduped_papers[] - DOI keyed"] DP --> SP["screened_papers[] - inclusion criteria"] SP --> CH["chunks[] - with span offsets"] CH --> RC["ranked_chunks[] - hybrid + rerank"] RC --> PI["paper_insights[] - 4-field schema"] PI --> VC["verified_claims[] - score, evidence"] VC --> TH["themes[] - cluster, contradictions, gaps"] TH --> DR["draft_sections[]"] DR --> FN["final_review + refs.bib + insights.csv"] VC -.->|"below threshold"| QP TH -.->|"thin coverage"| SQ ``` --- ## 7. Agent contracts Every agent subclasses `Agent` in `agents/base.py` and implements `run(state: ReviewState) -> dict` returning a **partial state update only**. Agents never mutate state in place. Every agent logs `{agent, iteration, input_hash, output_summary, tokens, latency}` to the trace. ### 7.1 Planner - **In:** `research_question`, `constraints`, optional `critic_feedback` - **Out:** `sub_questions[]` (4–8), `search_plan[]`, `taxonomy` (seeded from C1–C6), `inclusion_criteria` - **Behaviour:** decomposes by facet (method / application / evaluation / limitation). Emits per-sub-question source priority and year filters. On replan, must *change* the plan — record a diff, never re-emit an identical plan. ### 7.2 Retriever - **In:** `search_plan[]` - **Out:** `papers[]`, `chunks[]`, `retrieval_log` - **Behaviour:** 1. Federated search across enabled connectors; normalise to `Paper`. 2. Dedup by DOI → normalised title+year fallback. 3. Screen against `inclusion_criteria`; drop out-of-scope early (cheap LLM or heuristic). 4. Fetch OA PDFs where available; parse, chunk, embed, index. 5. Hybrid retrieve: dense (k=30) + BM25 (k=30) → RRF fuse → cross-encoder rerank → top-k=12 per sub-question. 6. Assign `venue_tier` via Citation Service. - **Rule:** never fabricate metadata. A field that cannot be resolved is `None`, not guessed. ### 7.3 Extractor - **In:** `papers[]`, `chunks[]` - **Out:** `paper_insights[]` - **Schema per paper (the four-field standard):** `methodology`, `advantages`, `disadvantages`, `critique` — plus `datasets`, `metrics`, `results`, `limitations`, `evidence_spans[]`. - **Rule:** every field carries `evidence_spans` (chunk_id + char offsets). No span → field is `null` with `extraction_note`. ### 7.4 Verifier - **In:** `paper_insights[]`, `chunks[]` - **Out:** `verified_claims[]`, `unsupported_claims[]`, `grounding_score` - **Behaviour:** decompose each insight into atomic claims; retrieve supporting evidence for each; NLI-style judgement → `SUPPORTED` / `PARTIAL` / `UNSUPPORTED` / `CONTRADICTED` with `support_score ∈ [0,1]`. Threshold default `0.7`. Cross-paper contradiction detection produces `contradiction_pairs[]`. - **Rule:** unsupported claims are **removed** from the write path and logged — never hedged into the output. ### 7.5 Critic - **In:** full state - **Out:** `decision ∈ {WRITE, RETRIEVE, REPLAN}`, `feedback`, `coverage_report` - **Checks:** sub-question coverage ≥ 80%; ≥ `min_papers` (default 20) retained; grounding_score ≥ 0.75; no sub-question with < 2 supporting papers; venue-tier mix acceptable; recency window satisfied. - **Loop control:** `max_iterations = 3`. On the final iteration force `WRITE` and record unresolved gaps in a *Limitations* section rather than looping forever. ### 7.6 Writer - **In:** verified state - **Out:** `review.md`, `review.docx`, `insights.csv`, `refs.bib` - **Structure:** Abstract · Introduction · Methodology of the review · Thematic sections (one per cluster) · Comparative insight table · Contradictions & open problems · Research gaps · Conclusion · References. - **Rules:** IEEE numeric citation style `[n]`. Every non-trivial sentence carries ≥1 citation. Preprints marked `[preprint]` in the reference list. No sentence may be written that is not backed by a `verified_claim`. --- ## 8. Core data models (`core/models.py`) ```python from typing import Literal, Optional from pydantic import BaseModel, Field VenueTier = Literal["scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"] Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"] Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"] class Paper(BaseModel): paper_id: str doi: Optional[str] = None title: str authors: list[str] = [] year: Optional[int] = None venue: Optional[str] = None venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown" abstract: Optional[str] = None url: Optional[str] = None pdf_path: Optional[str] = None source: str # openalex | s2 | arxiv | acl | ieee | scopus ... citation_count: Optional[int] = None is_preprint: bool = False class Chunk(BaseModel): chunk_id: str paper_id: str text: str section: Optional[str] = None # abstract | methods | results | ... start_char: int end_char: int embedding_id: Optional[str] = None class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel): chunk_id: str quote: str start_char: int end_char: int class PaperInsight(BaseModel): paper_id: str methodology: Optional[str] = None advantages: Optional[str] = None disadvantages: Optional[str] = None critique: Optional[str] = None datasets: list[str] = [] metrics: list[str] = [] results: Optional[str] = None limitations: Optional[str] = None cluster: Optional[str] = None # C1..C6 evidence_spans: list[EvidenceSpan] = [] extraction_note: Optional[str] = None class Claim(BaseModel): claim_id: str text: str paper_ids: list[str] verdict: Verdict support_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0) evidence: list[EvidenceSpan] = [] class SubQuestion(BaseModel): sq_id: str text: str facet: str # method | application | evaluation | limitation covered: bool = False supporting_paper_ids: list[str] = [] class SearchTask(BaseModel): sq_id: str query: str sources: list[str] year_min: Optional[int] = None max_results: int = 25 ``` ### 8.1 Graph state (`graph/state.py`) ```python from typing import Annotated, TypedDict from operator import add class ReviewState(TypedDict, total=False): # input research_question: str constraints: dict # years, venues, max_papers, language # planner sub_questions: list[SubQuestion] search_plan: list[SearchTask] inclusion_criteria: list[str] # retriever papers: Annotated[list[Paper], add] chunks: Annotated[list[Chunk], add] retrieval_log: Annotated[list[dict], add] # extractor / verifier paper_insights: list[PaperInsight] verified_claims: list[Claim] unsupported_claims: list[Claim] contradiction_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] grounding_score: float # critic decision: str critic_feedback: str coverage_report: dict iteration: int # writer themes: list[dict] draft_sections: dict final_review: str artefacts: dict ``` --- ## 9. Graph assembly (`graph/build.py`) ```python from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, START, END def route_after_critic(state: ReviewState) -> str: if state.get("iteration", 0) >= MAX_ITERATIONS: return "writer" return {"WRITE": "writer", "RETRIEVE": "retriever", "REPLAN": "planner"}[state["decision"]] g = StateGraph(ReviewState) g.add_node("planner", planner_node) g.add_node("retriever", retriever_node) g.add_node("extractor", extractor_node) g.add_node("verifier", verifier_node) g.add_node("critic", critic_node) g.add_node("writer", writer_node) g.add_edge(START, "planner") g.add_edge("planner", "retriever") g.add_edge("retriever", "extractor") g.add_edge("extractor", "verifier") g.add_edge("verifier", "critic") g.add_conditional_edges("critic", route_after_critic, {"writer": "writer", "retriever": "retriever", "planner": "planner"}) g.add_edge("writer", END) app = g.compile(checkpointer=SqliteSaver.from_conn_string("./data/checkpoints.db")) ``` State diagram: ```mermaid stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Planning Planning --> Retrieving Retrieving --> Extracting Extracting --> Verifying Verifying --> Critiquing Critiquing --> Writing: approved / max iterations Critiquing --> Retrieving: coverage gap Critiquing --> Planning: plan flawed Writing --> [*] ``` --- ## 10. Repository layout ``` researchgpt/ ├── CLAUDE.md ├── RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md ├── pyproject.toml ├── .env.example ├── configs/ │ ├── default.yaml │ ├── local_gemma.yaml │ └── eval.yaml ├── src/researchgpt/ │ ├── core/ llm.py config.py models.py logging.py prompts/ │ ├── data/ ingest.py chunker.py embeddings.py vectorstore.py bm25_index.py metadata_db.py │ ├── tools/ search_sources.py hybrid_retriever.py reranker.py pdf_loader.py citation_tools.py │ ├── agents/ base.py planner.py retriever.py extractor.py verifier.py critic.py writer.py │ ├── graph/ state.py build.py routing.py checkpoint.py │ ├── output/ markdown_writer.py docx_writer.py bibtex_writer.py insight_table.py │ ├── eval/ metrics.py ragas_runner.py ablations.py │ ├── api/ app.py schemas.py │ └── cli.py ├── tests/ unit/ integration/ fixtures/ cassettes/ ├── data/ raw/ pdfs/ vectorstore/ metadata.db checkpoints.db ├── outputs/ runs//{review.md,review.docx,insights.csv,refs.bib,trace.jsonl} └── notebooks/ 01_ingest.ipynb 02_retrieval_eval.ipynb 03_ablations.ipynb ``` ### 10.1 Config (`configs/default.yaml`) ```yaml llm: provider: openai # openai | anthropic | ollama model: gpt-4o-mini planner_model: gpt-4o # heavier model for planning + critique temperature: 0.1 max_tokens: 4096 embeddings: model: BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 device: cpu retrieval: dense_k: 30 sparse_k: 30 fusion: rrf rerank: true reranker: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 final_k: 12 chunk_size: 1200 chunk_overlap: 200 sources: enabled: [openalex, semantic_scholar, arxiv, crossref] optional: [ieee, scopus, acl, openreview, pmlr] max_per_source: 25 review: min_papers: 20 max_papers: 60 year_min: 2019 max_iterations: 3 grounding_threshold: 0.7 coverage_threshold: 0.8 output: citation_style: ieee formats: [markdown, docx, csv, bibtex] ``` --- ## 11. Retrieval design - **Chunking:** section-aware. Split on GROBID/heuristic section boundaries first, then recursive character split at 1200/200. Never merge across papers. Preserve `start_char`/`end_char` for grounding. - **Hybrid search:** dense (cosine) + BM25, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion `score = Σ 1/(60 + rank_i)`. - **Reranking:** cross-encoder over the fused top-60 → top-12. - **Query expansion:** Planner emits 2–3 paraphrases per sub-question; union results before fusion. - **Venue tiering:** boost `scopus_q1 > scopus/ieee/acl > peer_reviewed > preprint`. Applied as a score multiplier, not a hard filter, so strong preprints survive but rank below peer-reviewed work. - **Dedup:** DOI → normalised `title|year` → embedding cosine > 0.97 on title+abstract. --- ## 12. Evaluation protocol | Metric | Definition | Target | |---|---|---| | Retrieval Recall@k | Fraction of gold papers found in top-k | ≥ 0.80 | | Precision@k | Relevant among retrieved | ≥ 0.70 | | Citation accuracy | Citations resolving to a real paper that supports the claim | ≥ 0.95 | | Groundedness | Sentences with ≥1 supporting span | ≥ 0.90 | | Coverage | Sub-questions with ≥2 supporting papers | ≥ 0.80 | | Extraction F1 | Four-field extraction vs. human annotation on 20 papers | ≥ 0.75 | | Hallucination rate | Claims marked UNSUPPORTED that reach output | 0 by construction; report attempts | | Cost / latency | Tokens and wall-clock per review | Reported | **Ablations (required for the paper):** 1. Full system (all six agents). 2. − Critic loop (single pass). 3. − Verifier (no grounding filter). 4. − Agentic planning (single flat query). 5. − Hybrid retrieval (dense only). 6. − Reranker. 7. Baseline: vanilla RAG ≈ base paper configuration. **Human evaluation:** 3 annotators, 5 reviews, 5-point Likert on coverage / correctness / coherence / usefulness; report Krippendorff's α. Also run RAGAS (faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall) as an automated cross-check. --- ## 13. Build order | Phase | Deliverable | Done when | |---|---|---| | **0. Scaffold** | Repo, pyproject, config loader, LLM adapter, logging, `Paper`/`Chunk` models, CLI stub | `researchgpt --version` runs; adapter returns a completion from both hosted and Ollama | | **1. Ingestion + index** | Source connectors (OpenAlex, S2, arXiv, Crossref), PDF parse, chunk, embed, Chroma + BM25 | Query returns ranked chunks with correct span offsets | | **2. Hybrid retrieval** | RRF fusion, reranker, venue tiering, dedup | Recall@20 ≥ 0.8 on a 30-paper gold set | | **3. Agents (linear)** | Planner → Retriever → Extractor → Writer wired in LangGraph, no loop | End-to-end run produces a cited draft | | **4. Verification** | Verifier agent, claim decomposition, support scoring, unsupported filtering | Groundedness ≥ 0.9 on a sample | | **5. Agentic loop** | Critic agent, conditional edges, checkpointing, iteration cap | Loop demonstrably triggers and terminates on a deliberately under-covered query | | **6. Output + eval** | DOCX/BibTeX/CSV writers, metrics, ablation runner, optional Streamlit UI | Ablation table reproducible from one command | | **7. Paper support** | Figures from real traces, results tables, reproducibility script | `make reproduce` regenerates all reported numbers | --- ## 14. Rules for the coding agent 1. **Typed boundaries.** All agent I/O validates through Pydantic. A validation failure is an error, not a warning. 2. **No silent fabrication.** If metadata, a DOI, or a supporting span cannot be resolved, emit `None` and log. Never invent a citation, author, year, or venue. 3. **Partial state updates only.** Agents return dicts merged by LangGraph reducers. 4. **Prompts live in `core/prompts/` as versioned files**, not inline strings. Each prompt file has a header comment stating its agent, version, and expected output schema. 5. **Every LLM call goes through `core/llm.py`.** No direct SDK imports in agent modules. 6. **Deterministic tests.** Record fixtures with `vcrpy`; CI never hits a live API or a paid endpoint. 7. **Bounded loops.** Any retry, replan, or re-retrieve path must have an explicit cap and a forced exit. 8. **Cost guardrails.** Track tokens per run; abort with a clear error above `max_cost_usd` in config. 9. **Respect source terms.** Honour rate limits and robots; use official APIs; store only OA PDFs locally. 10. **Reproducibility.** Every run writes `outputs/runs//` containing config snapshot, trace, and artefacts. --- ## 15. Known risks and mitigations | Risk | Mitigation | |---|---| | Paywalled PDFs limit full-text extraction | Abstract-only degraded mode; flag `text_availability` per paper and report the split | | API rate limits / key gating (Scopus, IEEE) | Keyless sources are the default path; keyed connectors behind flags | | Loop non-termination or oscillation | Hard `max_iterations`; require plan diff on replan; forced WRITE on final iteration | | Cost blow-up from long contexts | Small model for extraction, large model for planning/critique; rerank before sending to LLM | | Local Gemma underperforms on structured extraction | Validate the architecture on a strong hosted model first; treat local swap as an ablation, not the baseline | | Extraction schema drift across papers | Strict Pydantic schema + retry-with-repair on parse failure, max 2 repairs | | Reviewer objection: "just RAG with extra steps" | Ablations 2–5 exist specifically to quantify each agent's contribution | --- ## 16. Open decisions - Vector store: stay on Chroma or move to Qdrant before Phase 6? - Whether to run GROBID (better structure, heavier setup) or PyMuPDF-only heuristics. - Gemma integration timing — after Phase 5 stabilises, as an ablation row. - Whether the Streamlit UI is in scope for the paper or deferred. --- *Last updated: 2026-08-06. Amend this file rather than duplicating spec text elsewhere.*

I've read through `RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md`. Here's my understanding of the project:

**What it is:** ResearchGPT — a multi-agent agentic RAG system that automates literature review generation. It's positioned as an extension of a base paper (Aytar et al. 2025, RAG-based literature assistance), meant to be both a working system and the basis for an academic paper.

**Core architecture:** Six agents orchestrated via LangGraph as a stateful graph with a feedback loop (not a fixed pipeline):
- **Planner** — decomposes the research question into sub-questions + a search plan
- **Retriever** — federated search (OpenAlex, S2, arXiv, Crossref, etc.), dedup, hybrid retrieval (dense + BM25, RRF fusion, cross-encoder rerank)
- **Extractor** — pulls a structured 4-field schema per paper (Methodology/Advantages/Disadvantages/Critique) with evidence spans
- **Verifier** — grounds every claim to a retrieved chunk, scores support, drops unsupported claims (never hedges)
- **Critic** — quality gate; decides WRITE / RETRIEVE / REPLAN, bounded to 3 iterations, forces WRITE on the last one
- **Writer** — synthesizes the final review (Markdown/DOCX/BibTeX/CSV) with IEEE-style citations, every claim traceable

**Key non-negotiables:**
1. Every claim must trace to a retrieved chunk — unsupported claims are dropped, not softened
2. Peer-reviewed sources outrank preprints (soft ranking boost, not hard filter)
3. Truly agentic — critic can loop back to planner/retriever, capped at 3 iterations
4. Model-agnostic LLM layer via LiteLLM (swap GPT/Claude/local Gemma without touching agent code)

**Stack:** LangGraph + LangChain, Pydantic v2 for typed I/O, Chroma→Qdrant vector store, BM25 hybrid retrieval, PyMuPDF/GROBID for PDFs, FastAPI+Streamlit (optional UI).

**Build order** is staged in 7 phases: scaffold → ingestion/index → hybrid retrieval → linear agent pipeline → verification → full agentic loop → output/eval → paper support. Status per the doc: **literature review is done, implementation hasn't started — build from Phase 0.**

There's also a full evaluation protocol (recall/precision, citation accuracy, groundedness, coverage, extraction F1, ablation study across 7 configurations) since this doubles as a research contribution.

## Repository Overview

SciReviewGen is the official dataset repository for "SciReviewGen: A Large-scale Dataset for Automatic Literature Review Generation," which proposes Query-weighted Fusion-in-Decoder (QFiD) that explicitly considers the relevance of each input document to the queries.

**Repository URL:** https://github.com/tetsu9923/SciReviewGen

## Dataset Details

SciReviewGen consists of over 10,000 literature reviews and 690,000 papers cited in the reviews. SciReviewGen is created based on S2ORC.

## License and Usage

SciReviewGen is released under CC BY-NC 4.0, and you can use SciReviewGen for only non-commercial purposes.

## Getting Started

To clone the repository and install the required packages, run: `git clone https://github.com/tetsu9923/SciReviewGen.git`, change into the directory, and then `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

## Publication

The dataset was introduced in a paper published at ACL 2023 (Findings) by Tetsu Kasanishi, Masaru Isonuma, Junichiro Mori, and Ichiro Sakata.

content.content:
# SciReviewGen Repository Overview

## Repository Structure
The repository contains preprocessing scripts, dataset files, and a QFiD model implementation. Key files include:
- `json_to_df.py` - Converts S2ORC data to dataframe format
- `make_section_df.py` - Constructs the main dataset
- `make_summarization_csv.py` - Generates CSV files for summarization tasks
- `qfid/` directory - Contains Query-weighted Fusion-in-Decoder code

## Data Format

**Core Datasets:**
- `split_survey_df`: Literature review chapters designed for generation tasks
- `original_survey_df`: Complete literature review texts
- `summarization_csv`: Formatted for summarization model training

**Fields per Example:**
- `paper_id`, `title`, `abstract` (review metadata)
- `section` (chapter title)
- `text` (review body)
- `n_bibs`, `n_nonbibs` (citation counts)
- `bib_titles`, `bib_abstracts` (cited paper information)
- `bib_citing_sentences` (contextual citations)
- `split` (train/val/test designation)

## Data Distribution & Creation

The dataset derives from S2ORC (2020-07-05 release). Three-step pipeline:

1. **Preprocessing**: Downloads S2ORC; runs `json_to_df.py` with field filtering (default: Computer Science)
2. **Construction**: Executes `make_section_df.py` with version selection
3. **CSV Generation**: Runs `make_summarization_csv.py`; optional `--for_qfid` flag for QFiD training

## License Terms

"SciReviewGen is released under CC BY-NC 4.0." Non-commercial use only. The dataset builds on S2ORC, which shares identical licensing restrictions.

## QFiD Baseline Model

The repository provides training/testing scripts in the `qfid/` directory. The approach "explicitly considers the relevance of each input document to the queries," distinguishing it from standard fusion-based methods.

content.text:
## SciReviewGen — what it is

**Paper:** Kasanishi et al., ACL 2023 Findings — *"SciReviewGen: A Large-scale Dataset for Automatic Literature Review Generation"* ([arXiv:2305.15186](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15186))
**Repo:** [tetsu9923/SciReviewGen](https://github.com/tetsu9923/SciReviewGen)

- Built from **S2ORC** (2020-07-05 snapshot): >10,000 literature review papers + ~690,000 papers they cite.
- Per chapter/section, you get: `title`, `abstract`, `section`, `text` (the human-written review chapter), plus `bib_titles`, `bib_abstracts`, `bib_citing_sentences`, `n_bibs`/`n_nonbibs`, and a `train/val/test` split.
- Baseline model: **QFiD** (Query-weighted Fusion-in-Decoder), a fine-tuned summarization model — a different paradigm from our prompted-agent architecture.
- Reported weakness: hallucination and shallow detail in generated reviews — which is exactly the failure mode our Verifier/Critic agents exist to prevent.
- **License: CC BY-NC 4.0**, non-commercial only (inherited from S2ORC).

## Where it fits — and where it doesn't

**Good fit: evaluation, not the live pipeline.**

| Spec section | How SciReviewGen helps |
|---|---|
| §13 Phase 2 ("Recall@20 ≥ 0.8 on a 30-paper gold set") | Each chapter's `bib_titles`/`bib_abstracts` is a ready-made query→gold-papers relevance set. Can replace/supplement hand-curated gold sets at scale, and it's static data so it satisfies the "no live API in CI" rule (§14.6) automatically. |
| §12 Retrieval Recall/Precision@k | Same — chapter topic as query, its cited papers as gold relevant set. |
| §12 Coverage / groundedness sanity check | Human-written chapter text gives a reference to compare generated draft sections against (ROUGE/BERTScore/LLM-judge), as an extra automatic cross-check alongside RAGAS. |
| §12 Baseline "vanilla RAG ≈ base paper configuration" ablation | Gives a second, external point of comparison beyond your own baseline run. |

**Bad fit — don't use it for:**
- **Live retrieval/generation.** The S2ORC snapshot is frozen at mid-2020; it can't satisfy the recency window (`year_min: 2019`, current queries) or the "no fabricated metadata" rule for anything published since. It's a static benchmark, not a source connector.
- **Extraction F1 (§12).** SciReviewGen has no methodology/advantages/disadvantages/critique labels per paper — you'd still need the planned 20-paper human annotation for that metric.
- **Fine-tuning a model.** The spec's architecture is prompt-driven agents over LiteLLM, not a trained summarizer like QFiD. Pulling in QFiD would be a different research direction, not an extension of this one.
- **Redistribution.** CC BY-NC 4.0 is fine for your academic/non-commercial use, but don't bundle the derived S2ORC text into a public repo — treat it as an external, license-gated eval dependency (download script + cache, not a committed artifact).

## Recommendation

Incorporate it narrowly, as an **evaluation-only asset** used in Phase 2 and Phase 6/7 (`researchgpt/eval/`) — a script that samples chapters (ideally filtered to topics overlapping your C1–C6 clusters) and builds a gold `query → papers[] → reference_text` set for retrieval-recall and coverage benchmarking. It strengthens your reproducibility story ("evaluated against an established external benchmark, not just self-curated gold sets") without touching the live agent graph.
